## Goals

Included here are analyses of morphological phenotypes in East Asian Zosterops taken from linear measurements of museum skins at the Cincinnati Museum Center, National Museum of Natural History at the Smithsonian, the American Museum of Natural History, and the Field Museum of Natural History.

## Getting started

We are using R version 4.5.2 and RStudio version 2026.05.1 for the analysis. Quarto version 1.6.39 for Mac OS was used to document the workflow. Set the working directory in RStudio to one where the `Zosterops_linear_measurements.csv` data file is accessible.

## General methods summary

Linear morphometric data including culmen length, nares-to-tip bill length, bill depth, bill width, tarsus length, wing cord, and tail length were collected from 388 round museum skins for all the Zosterops taxa in this study from the American Museum of Natural History (New York, NY, USA), Cincinnati Museum Center (Cincinnati, OH, USA), The Field Museum (Chicago, IL, USA), and the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History (Washington DC, USA). All measurements were recorded by the same researcher (HLM) in mm using either digital calipers or a wing rule. Culmen length was measured as exposed culmen from the tip of the bill to the point where the bill meets the forehead plumage. Bill length from nares-to-tip was measured from the distal end of the right nare to the tip of the bill. Bill depth and width were measured at the nares. Tarsus (tarsometatarsus) length was measured from the base of the phalanges to the tibiotarsal joint. Wing cord was measured unflattened with a wing rule. Tail length was measured from the body to the tip of the longest rectrix by placing the same wing rule in the center of the tail. Skins where poor condition or positioning prevented accurate measurements for one or more traits were excluded from analysis making the final analyzed dataset 354 individual specimens.

A PCA was conducted using the `prcomp` function and plotted for PC1-2 and for PC1-3 using *plotly* in R with specimens grouped solely according to species. Specimens were further divided into 11 groups for pairwise statistics including a 'continental' group of *Z. japonicus* specimens from the main islands of Japan, the Ryukyu Archipelago, and the Korean Peninsula and surrounding islands, an 'oceanic' *Z. japonicus* group including those subspecies *stejnegeri* and *alani* on oceanic islands in the Pacific (Izu, Ogasawara, and Volcano Islands), two *Z. montanus* groups including a northern Philippine group on the islands of Luzon and Mindoro, and a southern *Z. montanus* group in the central and southern Philippines and Indonesia, and the *Z. nigrorum catarmanensis* subspecies on the Philippine island of Camiguin South. The remaining samples, *Z. erythropleurus*, *Z. everetti*, *Z. meyeni*, *Z. nigrorum* (excluding *catarmanesnis*), *Z. palpebrosus*, and *Z. simplex*, were each grouped according to species. Box-and-whisker plots were generated for both grouping schemas, solely by species and by a combination of geography and species, tests for normality were conducted, and pairwise Wilcoxon tests were conducted for each pair of groups.

## Data files

### Final morphometric dataset

Morphological data for this analysis is in the comma delimited file titled `Zosterops_linear_measurements2.csv`. Import the morphological dataset using `read.csv` and summarize. In total 388 individual specimens were measured. Measurements for 354 skins were retained for analysis.

```{r}
#| label: Load data from .csv file.
# Import data from CSV file
ZosteropsMorph <- read.csv('./Data/Morphometrics/Zosterops_linear_measurements2.csv')
summary(ZosteropsMorph)
```

Create a table displaying all the data in the file `Zosterops_linear_measurements.csv`.

```{r}
#| label: Table for morphometric dataset.
ZosteropsMorph %>%
  gt(auto_align = FALSE)
```

## Principal component analyses (PCA)

### PCA for species

Conduct a principal component analysis (PCA) in which the groupings are species. Plot the first two principal components (PCs) and the first three PCs, with the percent of variance explained by each PC on the axes. Then plot PCs 1–3 once for each of four comparisons in which the *Z. japonicus* samples are highlighted in black and one other species (*Z. meyeni*, *Z. montanus*, *Z. simplex*, or *Z. palpebrosus*) in grey, keeping all other taxa as open circles. Each of these plots has a label with a leader line pointing to the *Z. japonicus* cloud and to the cloud of the comparison species. All 3D plots use the same camera position so that they can be compared side by side.

```{r}
#| label: PCA for species.
# Group data by 'species' and select relevant variables for PCA
ZosteropsMorph_species <- ZosteropsMorph %>% 
  select(Species, BillCulmen, BillNareTip, BillDepth, BillWidth, Tarsus, Wing, Tail) %>%
  group_by(Species)

# Perform PCA on the selected variables
pca_result <- prcomp(ZosteropsMorph_species[, -1], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Percent of variance explained by each PC
PCA_VARexp <- 100 * pca_result$sdev^2 / sum(pca_result$sdev^2)
round(PCA_VARexp, 1)
PC_title <- function(i) sprintf("PC%d (%.1f%%)", i, PCA_VARexp[i])

# Convert PCA result to a data frame for plotting and add 'Species'
pca_data <- as.data.frame(pca_result$x)
pca_data$Species <- ZosteropsMorph_species$Species

# Shared camera position for all 3D plots
PCA_camera <- list(eye = list(x = 1.25, y = 1.25, z = 1.25))
```

Plot PCs 1–2 and PCs 1–3 for all species.

```{r}
#| label: Plot PCs 1-2 and PCs 1-3 for all species.
ColorPal_CUSTOM <- c("#004949", "#DB6D00", "#D82632", "#FED439", "#FA9C88", "#924900", "#8DB6CD", "#008600")

PC2Dplot <- plot_ly(x = pca_data$PC1, y = pca_data$PC2, type = "scatter", mode = 'markers',
                    marker = list(size = 14, line = list(color = 'black', width = 1)),
                    color = pca_data$Species, colors = ColorPal_CUSTOM) %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(title = PC_title(1)),
         yaxis = list(title = PC_title(2)))
PC2Dplot

PC3Dplot <- plot_ly(x = pca_data$PC1, y = pca_data$PC2, z = pca_data$PC3,
                    type = "scatter3d", mode = 'markers',
                    marker = list(size = 14, line = list(color = 'black', width = 1)),
                    color = pca_data$Species, colors = ColorPal_CUSTOM) %>%
  layout(scene = list(xaxis = list(title = PC_title(1)),
                      yaxis = list(title = PC_title(2)),
                      zaxis = list(title = PC_title(3)),
                      camera = PCA_camera))
PC3Dplot
```

Plot PCs 1–3 comparing *Z. japonicus* (black) with each of four species (grey). Each label points to the specimen closest to that species' centroid on PCs 1–3. The label offsets (`jap_ax`, `jap_ay`, `comp_ax`, `comp_ay`, in pixels) can be changed for any plot in which a label sits on top of points.

```{r}
#| label: Plot PCs 1-3 comparing Z. japonicus with other species.
# Specimen closest to a species' centroid on PCs 1-3; used as the anchor for its label
label_point <- function(sp) {
  pts <- pca_data[pca_data$Species == sp, c("PC1", "PC2", "PC3")]
  pts[which.min(rowSums(sweep(as.matrix(pts), 2, colMeans(pts))^2)), ]
}
# Label with a leader line for one species' cloud
cloud_label <- function(sp, ax, ay) {
  pt <- label_point(sp)
  list(x = pt$PC1, y = pt$PC2, z = pt$PC3,
       text = sprintf("<i>Z. %s</i>", sp),
       showarrow = TRUE, arrowhead = 0, arrowwidth = 1.2, arrowcolor = "black",
       ax = ax, ay = ay, bgcolor = "white", font = list(size = 18, color = "black"))
}
# 3D plot of Z. japonicus (black) and one comparison species (grey); all other species open circles
PC3D_japonicus_vs <- function(comp, jap_ax = 90, jap_ay = -110, comp_ax = -120, comp_ay = 90) {
  marker_col <- ifelse(pca_data$Species == "japonicus", "black",
                       ifelse(pca_data$Species == comp, "grey", "transparent"))
  plot_ly(x = pca_data$PC1, y = pca_data$PC2, z = pca_data$PC3,
          type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers",
          marker = list(size = 10, color = marker_col, line = list(color = "black", width = 2)),
          text = pca_data$Species, hoverinfo = "text") %>%
    layout(scene = list(xaxis = list(title = PC_title(1)),
                        yaxis = list(title = PC_title(2)),
                        zaxis = list(title = PC_title(3)),
                        camera = PCA_camera,
                        annotations = list(cloud_label("japonicus", jap_ax, jap_ay),
                                           cloud_label(comp, comp_ax, comp_ay))),
           showlegend = FALSE)
}
PC3D_japo_meye <- PC3D_japonicus_vs("meyeni")
PC3D_japo_mont <- PC3D_japonicus_vs("montanus")
PC3D_japo_simp <- PC3D_japonicus_vs("simplex")
PC3D_japo_palp <- PC3D_japonicus_vs("palpebrosus", comp_ax = -100, comp_ay = 110)
PC3D_japo_meye
PC3D_japo_mont
PC3D_japo_simp
PC3D_japo_palp
```

Export the 3D plots as html files (open them in a browser and use the camera icon to save an image).

```{r}
#| label: Export the 3D PCA plots for species as html files.
saveWidget(PC3Dplot, file = "Zosterops3DPCAplot_morph_ALL.html")
saveWidget(PC3D_japo_meye, file = "Zosterops3DPCAplot_morph_japo_meye.html")
saveWidget(PC3D_japo_mont, file = "Zosterops3DPCAplot_morph_japo_mont.html")
saveWidget(PC3D_japo_simp, file = "Zosterops3DPCAplot_morph_japo_simp.html")
saveWidget(PC3D_japo_palp, file = "Zosterops3DPCAplot_morph_japo_palp.html")
```

### Morphological and genetic distances between species

For PCs 1-3 calculate the centroids and Euclidean distances for pairwise comparisons between species.

```{r}
#| label: Calculate the centroids and Euclidean pairwise distances.
# Initialize an empty data frame to store centroids
ZosteropsMorph_PCAcentroids <- data.frame(Group = character(), PC1 = numeric(), PC2 = numeric(), PC3 = numeric(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Loop through each unique species to calculate centroids
for (species in unique(pca_data$Species)) {
  group_scores <- pca_data[pca_data$Species == species, 1:3]  # Select PCA scores for the species
  centroid <- colMeans(group_scores, na.rm = TRUE)  # Calculate the centroid
  ZosteropsMorph_PCAcentroids <- rbind(ZosteropsMorph_PCAcentroids, 
                                        data.frame(Group = species, 
                                                   PC1 = centroid[1], 
                                                   PC2 = centroid[2], 
                                                   PC3 = centroid[3]))
}

# Print the centroids
print(ZosteropsMorph_PCAcentroids)
# Calculate the Euclidean distances between centroids
ZosteropsMorph_PCAdistance_matrix <- as.matrix(dist(ZosteropsMorph_PCAcentroids[, 2:4]))  # Exclude the Group column
ZosteropsMorph_PCAdistance_df <- as.data.frame(ZosteropsMorph_PCAdistance_matrix)

# Set row and column names for the distance data frame
rownames(ZosteropsMorph_PCAdistance_df) <- ZosteropsMorph_PCAcentroids$Group
colnames(ZosteropsMorph_PCAdistance_df) <- ZosteropsMorph_PCAcentroids$Group

# Print the distance data frame
print(ZosteropsMorph_PCAdistance_df)
```

For the PCA produced from the SNP data Euclidean distances were also calculated between species (see [**Distance trees, PCA, UMAP, and DAPC analyses**](https://hermmays.github.io/Zosterops1/ZosteropsSNPs_analysis.html)). Compare the genetic distances with those from the morphometric dataset using Spearman's ⍴. Because different groupings were used in the genetic versus morphometric PCAs in some cases we are using the mean genetic distance. For example, in the genetic PCA *Z. montanus* was divided into north, south, and Palawan groups. Here we are taking the mean from the genetic distances between those groups and using that in pairwise comparisons of genetic distance between *Z. montanus* and other species. Correlation analysis using Spearman's ⍴ between pairwise comparisons for genetic and morphological distance was calculated as follows. A plot of morphological and genetic distances was produced and pairwise comparisons involving *Z. japonicus* were highlighted (black points) from the remaining pairwise comparisons (open points).

```{r}
#| label: Spearman correlation between morphometric and genetic distances.
# Read the data from a CSV file
Zosterops_distance_data <- read.csv("Data/Morphometrics/Zosterops_genetic_morpho_dist.csv")

# Calculate the correlation for all comparisons using Spearman
correlation_all <- cor(Zosterops_distance_data$genetic_dist, Zosterops_distance_data$morpho_dist, method = "spearman")
print(paste("Correlation coefficient (all comparisons):", round(correlation_all, 3)))
# Perform a statistical significance test for all comparisons using Spearman
cor_test_all <- cor.test(Zosterops_distance_data$genetic_dist, Zosterops_distance_data$morpho_dist, method = "spearman")
print(cor_test_all)
# Filter data for JAPO comparisons
Zosterops_JAPO_data <- Zosterops_distance_data[grepl("JAPO", Zosterops_distance_data$pairwise_comp), ]

# Calculate the correlation for JAPO comparisons using Spearman
correlation_JAPO <- cor(Zosterops_JAPO_data$genetic_dist, Zosterops_JAPO_data$morpho_dist, method = "spearman")
print(paste("Correlation coefficient (JAPO comparisons):", round(correlation_JAPO, 3)))
# Perform a statistical significance test for JAPO comparisons using Spearman
cor_test_JAPO <- cor.test(Zosterops_JAPO_data$genetic_dist, Zosterops_JAPO_data$morpho_dist, method = "spearman")
print(cor_test_JAPO)
# Fit linear models for R-squared calculation
lm_model_all <- lm(morpho_dist ~ genetic_dist, data = Zosterops_distance_data)
r_squared_all <- summary(lm_model_all)$r.squared

lm_model_JAPO <- lm(morpho_dist ~ genetic_dist, data = Zosterops_JAPO_data)
r_squared_JAPO <- summary(lm_model_JAPO)$r.squared

# Plot the data
Zosterops_correlation_plot <- ggplot(Zosterops_distance_data, aes(x = genetic_dist, y = morpho_dist)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = ifelse(grepl("JAPO", pairwise_comp), "filled", "open")), size = 3, color = "black", show.legend = FALSE) +  # Points based on shape, no legend
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("open" = 1, "filled" = 16)) +  # Open circles and filled circles
  labs(
       x = "Genetic Distance",
       y = "Morphological Distance") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Display the plot
print(Zosterops_correlation_plot)
```

### PCA for *Z. japonicus* by region

Conduct a separate PCA on the *Z. japonicus* specimens only, grouped by region: continental (main islands of Japan, the Korean Peninsula, and the Ryukyu, Daito, and Osumi Islands), the Izu Islands (*Z. j. stejnegeri*), and the Ogasawara and Volcano Islands (*Z. j. alani*). Plot PCs 1–2 and PCs 1–3.

```{r}
#| label: PCA for Z. japonicus by region.
ZosteropsMorph_japonicus <- ZosteropsMorph %>%
  filter(Species == "japonicus") %>%
  mutate(Region = case_when(Subspecies == "stejnegeri" ~ "Izu Islands (stejnegeri)",
                            Subspecies == "alani"      ~ "Ogasawara/Volcano Islands (alani)",
                            TRUE                        ~ "Continental"),
         Region = factor(Region, levels = c("Continental", "Izu Islands (stejnegeri)",
                                            "Ogasawara/Volcano Islands (alani)")))
table(ZosteropsMorph_japonicus$Region)

pca_japonicus <- prcomp(ZosteropsMorph_japonicus[, c("BillCulmen", "BillNareTip", "BillDepth", "BillWidth",
                                                     "Tarsus", "Wing", "Tail")],
                        center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
PCA_VARexp_japonicus <- 100 * pca_japonicus$sdev^2 / sum(pca_japonicus$sdev^2)
round(PCA_VARexp_japonicus, 1)
round(pca_japonicus$rotation[, 1:3], 2)
PC_title_japonicus <- function(i) sprintf("PC%d (%.1f%%)", i, PCA_VARexp_japonicus[i])

pca_data_japonicus <- as.data.frame(pca_japonicus$x)
pca_data_japonicus$Region <- ZosteropsMorph_japonicus$Region

ColorPal_japonicus <- c("#D82632", "#8E1B22", "#290AD8")  # continental, Izu, Ogasawara/Volcano
```

```{r}
#| label: Plot PCs 1-2 and PCs 1-3 for Z. japonicus by region.
PC2D_japonicus <- plot_ly(x = pca_data_japonicus$PC1, y = pca_data_japonicus$PC2,
                          type = "scatter", mode = 'markers',
                          marker = list(size = 14, line = list(color = 'black', width = 1)),
                          color = pca_data_japonicus$Region, colors = ColorPal_japonicus) %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(title = PC_title_japonicus(1)),
         yaxis = list(title = PC_title_japonicus(2)))
PC2D_japonicus

PC3D_japonicus <- plot_ly(x = pca_data_japonicus$PC1, y = pca_data_japonicus$PC2, z = pca_data_japonicus$PC3,
                          type = "scatter3d", mode = 'markers',
                          marker = list(size = 10, line = list(color = 'black', width = 1)),
                          color = pca_data_japonicus$Region, colors = ColorPal_japonicus) %>%
  layout(scene = list(xaxis = list(title = PC_title_japonicus(1)),
                      yaxis = list(title = PC_title_japonicus(2)),
                      zaxis = list(title = PC_title_japonicus(3)),
                      camera = PCA_camera))
PC3D_japonicus

saveWidget(PC2D_japonicus, file = "Zosterops2DPCAplot_morph_japonicus_regions.html")
saveWidget(PC3D_japonicus, file = "Zosterops3DPCAplot_morph_japonicus_regions.html")
```

### PCA for subspecies

Conduct a PCA in which the groupings are subspecies. Only show a single plot for two PCs and all subspecies.

```{r}
#| label: Morphometric PCA for subspecies.
# Group data by 'Name' (subspecies) and select relevant variables for PCA
ZosteropsMorph_subspecies <- ZosteropsMorph %>%
  select(Name, BillCulmen, BillNareTip, BillDepth, BillWidth, Tarsus, Wing, Tail) %>%
  group_by(Name)

# Perform PCA on the selected variables
pca_result <- prcomp(ZosteropsMorph_subspecies[, -1], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Convert PCA result to a data frame for plotting
pca_data <- as.data.frame(pca_result$x)

# Add 'Name' variable to PCA data for coloring
pca_data$Name <- ZosteropsMorph_subspecies$Name

# Plot the first two principal components
ggplot(pca_data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Name)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) + 
  labs(title = "PCA of Zosterops Morphological Measurements",
       x = "Principal Component 1",
       y = "Principal Component 2") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())
```

## Box-and-whisker plots and pairwise tests

### Species plots and summaries

Define color values for box plots to match prior color schemes.

```{r}
#| label: Define color scheme for box-and-whisker plots.
species_colors <- c("#004949", "#DB6D00", "#D82632", "#FED439", "#FA9C88", "#924900", "#8DB6CD", "#008600")
```

Create box-and-whisker plots for each individual trait and every species.

```{r}
#| label: Box-and-whisker plots for species and each trait.
# Define a function to create boxplots for each trait
create_boxplot <- function(ZosteropsMorph_species, trait) {
  ggplot(ZosteropsMorph_species, aes_string(x = "Species", y = trait)) + 
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + # Boxplot without outliers
    geom_jitter(width = 0.2, aes(color = Species), size = 2, alpha = 0.5) + # Add jitter for individual points
    labs(title = paste("Boxplot of", trait, "by Species"), x = "Species", y = trait) + 
    scale_color_manual(values = species_colors) +
    theme_minimal() # Minimal theme for better aesthetics
}
# List of traits to plot
traits <- c("BillCulmen", "BillNareTip", "BillDepth", "BillWidth", "Tarsus", "Wing", "Tail")
# Loop through each trait and create boxplots
for (trait in traits) {
  print(create_boxplot(ZosteropsMorph_species, trait)) # Print each boxplot
}
```

Descriptive statistics for morphometric traits by species.

```{r}
#| label: Descriptive statistics for morphometric traits by species.
ZosteropsMorph_descriptive_stats_species <- ZosteropsMorph_species %>%
  select(Species, BillCulmen, BillNareTip, BillDepth, BillWidth, Tarsus, Wing, Tail) %>%  # Select relevant columns
  group_by(Species) %>%  # Group by 'Group'
  summarise(  # Summarize to get descriptive statistics
    Mean_BillCulmen = mean(BillCulmen, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_BillCulmen = median(BillCulmen, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_BillCulmen = sd(BillCulmen, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    Mean_BillNareTip = mean(BillNareTip, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_BillNareTip = median(BillNareTip, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_BillNareTip = sd(BillNareTip, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    Mean_BillDepth = mean(BillDepth, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_BillDepth = median(BillDepth, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_BillDepth = sd(BillDepth, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    Mean_BillWidth = mean(BillWidth, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_BillWidth = median(BillWidth, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_BillWidth = sd(BillWidth, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    Mean_Tarsus = mean(Tarsus, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Tarsus = median(Tarsus, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Tarsus = sd(Tarsus, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    Mean_Wing = mean(Wing, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Wing = median(Wing, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Wing = sd(Wing, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    Mean_Tail = mean(Tail, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Tail = median(Tail, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Tail = sd(Tail, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
# View the descriptive statistics table
print(ZosteropsMorph_descriptive_stats_species)
write.csv(ZosteropsMorph_descriptive_stats_species)
ZosteropsMorph_descriptive_stats_species %>%
  gt(auto_align = FALSE)
```

### Taxonomic/biogeographic group plots, summaries, and t-tests

Define colors for box-and-whisker plots for taxonomic/biogeographic groups.

```{r}
#| label: Define the color schemes for taxonomic/biogeographic groups.
group_colors <- c("#004949", "#DB6D00", "#D82632", "#290AD8", "#FED439", "#B66DFF", "#FA9C88", "#924900", "#CDAA7D", "#8DB6CD", "#008600")
```

Test each trait within each taxonomic/biogeographic group for normality.

```{r}
#| label: Test each morphometric trait for normality.
# Select relevant variables and group by taxonomic group separating montanus into NORTH and SOUTH groups and japonicus into CONTINENTAL and OCEANIC groups and create datasets with the original data and log transformed data. 
ZosteropsMorph_groups <- ZosteropsMorph %>%
  select(Group, BillCulmen, BillNareTip, BillDepth, BillWidth, Tarsus, Wing, Tail) %>%
  group_by(Group)

# Function to perform Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for each variable within each group
perform_ks_test <- function(group_data, variable) {
  # Create a list to store results
  results <- list()
  
  # Get unique groups
  unique_groups <- unique(group_data$Group)
  
  # Iterate over each unique group
  for (i in 1:length(unique_groups)) {
    # Filter data for the specific group
    group_name <- unique_groups[i]
    group_values <- group_data %>% filter(Group == group_name) %>% pull(variable)
    
    # Perform KS test with the first group's data as reference
    if (i == 1) {
      reference_values <- group_values
    } else {
      ks_test_result <- ks.test(group_values, reference_values)
      results[[group_name]] <- ks_test_result
    }
  }
  return(results)
}
```

### Significance letters for box-and-whisker plots

Summarize the pairwise Wilcoxon tests (Bonferroni-corrected) as compact letter displays: groups that share a letter do not differ significantly (*p* ≥ 0.05) for that trait, and groups with no letter in common do. Letters are assigned in order of decreasing group mean, so "a" marks the group(s) with the largest values.

```{r}
#| label: Compact letter displays from the pairwise Wilcoxon tests.
morph_traits <- c("BillCulmen", "BillNareTip", "BillDepth", "BillWidth", "Tarsus", "Wing", "Tail")
WILCOX_tests <- list(BillCulmen = WILCOX_BillCulmen, BillNareTip = WILCOX_BillNareTip,
                     BillDepth = WILCOX_BillDepth, BillWidth = WILCOX_BillWidth,
                     Tarsus = WILCOX_Tarsus, Wing = WILCOX_Wing, Tail = WILCOX_Tail)

# Convert a pairwise.wilcox.test p-value matrix into a named vector ("group1-group2")
wilcox_pvector <- function(test) {
  pm <- test$p.value
  idx <- which(!is.na(pm), arr.ind = TRUE)
  setNames(pm[idx], paste(rownames(pm)[idx[, 1]], colnames(pm)[idx[, 2]], sep = "-"))
}

groups_df <- as.data.frame(ZosteropsMorph_groups)
CLD_groups <- bind_rows(lapply(morph_traits, function(trait) {
  pv <- wilcox_pvector(WILCOX_tests[[trait]])
  cld <- multcompLetters2(as.formula(paste(trait, "~ Group")), pv, groups_df, threshold = 0.05)
  data.frame(Trait = trait, Group = names(cld$Letters), Letters = unname(cld$Letters))
}))

# Number of significant pairs per trait, out of all pairwise comparisons
sapply(WILCOX_tests, function(t) sum(t$p.value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE))
CLD_groups %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Trait, values_from = Letters) %>%
  gt(auto_align = FALSE)
```

Box-and-whisker plots by taxonomic/biogeographic group with the significance letters above each box. Set `traits_shown` to plot a subset of traits (for example, `c("BillCulmen", "Tarsus", "Wing")`) for a smaller figure.

```{r}
#| label: Box-and-whisker plots by taxonomic/biogeographic group with significance letters.
#| fig-width: 18
#| fig-height: 25

# Traits to plot (use a subset, e.g. c("BillCulmen", "Tarsus", "Wing"), for a smaller figure)
traits_shown <- morph_traits
trait_titles <- c(BillCulmen = "Bill length culmen (mm)", BillNareTip = "Bill length nare-to-tip (mm)",
                  BillDepth = "Bill depth (mm)", BillWidth = "Bill width (mm)",
                  Tarsus = "Tarsus length (mm)", Wing = "Wing cord length (mm)", Tail = "Tail length (mm)")

# Group names for the legend (plotmath: italic species names)
grp_lab <- c(erythropleurus          = "italic('Z. erythropleurus')",
             everetti                = "italic('Z. everetti')",
             `japonicus CONTINENTAL` = "italic('Z. japonicus')~'continental'",
             `japonicus OCEANIC`     = "italic('Z. japonicus')~'oceanic'",
             meyeni                  = "italic('Z. meyeni')",
             `montanus NORTH`        = "italic('Z. montanus')~'N. Philippines'",
             `montanus SOUTH`        = "italic('Z. montanus')~'C./S. Philippines'",
             nigrorum                = "italic('Z. nigrorum')",
             `nigrorum CS`           = "italic('Z. n. catarmanensis')",
             palpebrosus             = "italic('Z. palpebrosus')",
             simplex                 = "italic('Z. simplex')")

boxplot_with_letters <- function(trait, tag) {
  # Letters sit just above the highest point of each group
  tops <- groups_df %>% group_by(Group) %>% summarise(y = max(.data[[trait]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  pad <- 0.05 * diff(range(groups_df[[trait]], na.rm = TRUE))
  lab <- CLD_groups %>% filter(Trait == trait) %>% left_join(tops, by = "Group") %>% mutate(y = y + pad)
  ggplot(groups_df, aes(x = Group, y = .data[[trait]])) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_jitter(aes(color = Group), width = 0.2, size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_text(data = lab, aes(x = Group, y = y, label = Letters), size = 6, vjust = 0) +
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = tag, hjust = 1.3, vjust = 1.3, size = 12) +
    scale_color_manual(values = group_colors, name = "Group",
                       labels = function(b) parse(text = grp_lab[b])) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 1.3))) +   # room on the right for the panel letter
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 5, alpha = 1))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = trait_titles[[trait]]) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = element_text(size = 19),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15),
          legend.title = element_text(size = 22),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0),
          panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1))
}

panel_tags <- paste0(letters[seq_along(traits_shown)], ".")
boxplots_letters <- mapply(boxplot_with_letters, traits_shown, panel_tags, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

# Two columns, with the shared legend in the next empty cell (bottom right for seven traits)
ZosteropsMorph_groups_letters <- wrap_plots(c(boxplots_letters, list(guide_area())), ncol = 2) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect")
ZosteropsMorph_groups_letters
ggsave("Zosterops_morph_boxplots_letters.pdf", ZosteropsMorph_groups_letters, width = 18, height = 25)
```

Summary table of group means ± standard errors with the significance letters as superscripts.

```{r}
#| label: Table of group means and standard errors with significance letters.
Morph_summary_letters <- groups_df %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(morph_traits), names_to = "Trait", values_to = "Value") %>%
  group_by(Group, Trait) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(Value)), Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            SE = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(CLD_groups, by = c("Group", "Trait")) %>%
  mutate(Cell = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f<sup>%s</sup>", Mean, SE, Letters)) %>%
  select(Group, n, Trait, Cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Trait, values_from = Cell) %>%
  select(Group, n, all_of(morph_traits))   # keep the traits in the usual order

# Group names as they appear in the manuscript (markdown: *italic*)
group_names_md <- c(erythropleurus          = "*Z. erythropleurus*",
                    everetti                = "*Z. everetti*",
                    `japonicus CONTINENTAL` = "*Z. japonicus* continental",
                    `japonicus OCEANIC`     = "*Z. japonicus* oceanic",
                    meyeni                  = "*Z. meyeni*",
                    `montanus NORTH`        = "*Z. montanus* N. Philippines",
                    `montanus SOUTH`        = "*Z. montanus* C./S. Philippines and Indonesia",
                    nigrorum                = "*Z. nigrorum*",
                    `nigrorum CS`           = "*Z. n. catarmanensis* (Camiguin South)",
                    palpebrosus             = "*Z. palpebrosus*",
                    simplex                 = "*Z. simplex*")

# Caption, written from the data so the counts stay correct if the dataset changes
Morph_table_caption <- paste0(
  "**Table 1.** Means ± standard errors (mm) of seven linear measurements from ",
  sum(Morph_summary_letters$n), " museum study skins, by taxonomic/biogeographic group. ",
  "Superscript letters summarize pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum tests with Bonferroni correction for each measurement: ",
  "groups that share a letter do not differ significantly (*p* ≥ 0.05), and \"a\" marks the group with the largest values. ",
  "*Z. japonicus* continental includes the main islands of Japan, the Korean Peninsula and adjacent islands, and the Ryukyu Archipelago; ",
  "*Z. japonicus* oceanic includes *Z. j. stejnegeri* (Izu Islands) and *Z. j. alani* (Volcano Islands and Minamitorishima); ",
  "*Z. montanus* N. Philippines includes Luzon and Mindoro; *Z. montanus* C./S. Philippines and Indonesia includes Panay, Negros, Mindanao, and Timor; ",
  "*Z. n. catarmanensis* (Camiguin South) is shown separately because phylogenetic analyses place it within *Z. montanus*. ",
  "Specimens from introduced populations were excluded.")

Morph_summary_gt <- Morph_summary_letters %>%
  gt() %>%
  text_transform(locations = cells_body(columns = Group),
                 fn = function(x) lapply(group_names_md[x], gt::md)) %>%
  text_transform(locations = cells_body(columns = all_of(morph_traits)),
                 fn = function(x) lapply(x, gt::html)) %>%
  cols_label(BillCulmen = "Culmen", BillNareTip = "Nare–tip", BillDepth = "Bill depth",
             BillWidth = "Bill width", Tarsus = "Tarsus", Wing = "Wing", Tail = "Tail") %>%
  tab_header(title = md(Morph_table_caption)) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_text(align = "left", size = "small"),
            locations = cells_title(groups = "title"))
Morph_summary_gt
gtsave(Morph_summary_gt, "Zosterops_morph_group_means_SE_letters.docx")

# Plain csv without the html superscript tags
Morph_summary_letters %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(morph_traits), ~ gsub("<sup>(.*)</sup>", " \\1", .x))) %>%
  write.csv("Zosterops_morph_group_means_SE_letters.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
